sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Accused No.4 in Crime No.354/2023 of Yeshwanthapura Police Station, has preferred this petition under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail.

2. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent/State and perused the material on record.
3.

The first informant Mr.Tilak.M has set the law into motion by lodging a complaint with respondent police on 06.11.2023, based on which the aforesaid mentioned case was registered against accused Nos.1 to 4 for the offence punishable under Section 506, 504, 420, 342 and 417 read with Section 34 of IPC.

4. The gist of the complaint averments are that, in the year 2014 the complainant came in contact with accused No.1 Smt. Kavitha Singh through a friend by NC: 2024:KHC:2216 name Manisha Venkatesh and the said accused introduced herself as the grand daughter of former Chief Minister,
late Sri. Dharmsingh and she is a DCP in Delhi etc.
5.
It is alleged that the complainant was made to spend lot of money and he was blackmailed and his marriage was performed with accused No.3.

Then, the accused persons extracted Crores of rupees and further demanded Rs.25,00,000/- stating that if the said amount was not paid, a false complaint will be lodged alleging rape etc.
6.
The petitioner is arraigned as accused No.4 in the FIR.
He is said to be the brother of accused No.1.

The allegations against the petitioner is that, when the complainant was in judicial custody in connection with a false case registered against him in Crime No.139/2022 and Crime No.140/2022,
the petitioner herein took a blank cheque for a sum of Rs.65,000/- belonging to the complainant,
which was kept in the house of Accused No.1 as well as the gold chain and bracelet and pledged the NC: 2024:KHC:2216 same in one SVC Co-operative bank and borrowed a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- in the guise of releasing him on bail and also took away a sum of Rs.14,00,000/- from the factory Kiran Singh K vs The State Of Karnataka on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180027226/
2 which he had kept for paying the factory workers, stating that the said amount has been spent for Courts expenditures.

sentences.text: 7. The main allegations are against accused No.1.

The allegation that when the complainant was in judicial custody, the petitioner took a cheque bearing No.171663 for a sum of Rs.65,000/- belonging to the complainant and also took his gold chain, bracelet etc. and pledged the same and received Rs.2,00,000/- form one SVC Co-operative bank and took away a sum of Rs.14,00,000/- from the factory etc., is a matter which has to be established in due course.
There was no complaint lodged alleging the same, immediately.
The petitioner has no criminal antecedents.
In the said facts and circumstances, the relief sought by the petitioner can be granted by imposing conditions.

Accordingly, the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:2216 ORDER i) Petition is allowed.
ii) In the event of arrest of the Petitioner/accused No.4 in Crime No.354/2023 of Yeshwanthapura Police Station, he shall be released subject to following conditions:
a) He shall appear before the Investigation Officer within a period of Ten days from the date of receipt of a copy of the order and shall execute a bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only) with two sureties for the likesum.

b) He shall furnish proof of his  residential address and shall inform the  Investigation Officer/Court, if there is any  change in the address.
 c) He shall be available for the purpose of investigation as and when required and shall co-operate with the investigation.
d) He shall not leave the jurisdiction of the trial Court without prior permission till completion of the investigation of the case.
NC: 2024:KHC:2216 e) He shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly.
f) He shall be regular in attending the Court proceedings.
